items.actClause:
AN ACT in relation to authorizing and empowering CREF to combine with TIAA,
with TIAA continuing in existence as the surviving entity following such
combination and with CREF ceasing to be a corporate entity; and to repeal
chapter 124 of the laws of 1952, relating to incorporating the college
retirement equities fund for the benefit of the teaching profession
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2679

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to authorizing and empowering CREF to combine with
TIAA, with TIAA continuing in existence as the surviving entity follow-
ing such combination and with CREF ceasing to be a corporate entity; and
to repeal chapter 124 of the laws of 1952, relating to incorporating the
college retirement equities fund for the benefit of the teaching profes-
sion

 
PURPOSE:

To allow for the combination of Teachers Insurance and Annuity Associ-
ation (TIAA) and the College Retirement Equities Fund (CREF).

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one provides for the repeal of Chapter 124 of the Laws of 1952
which established CREF. Section two establishes the definitions for this
act, which authorizes the combination of TIAA and CREF. Section three
authorizes the merger of TIAA and CREF, creates a new Separate account
within TIAA and establishes approvals by the respective TIAA and CREF
Boards of Governors and by the Department of Financial Services (DFS).
If approved by DFS, the plan of combination will be filed with the New
York County Clerk. Section four transfers all assets and liabilities,
including any causes of action or defenses, of CREF to TIAA. In addi-
tion, all contracts and certificates issued by CREF and in force at the
time of the combination, will become TIAA variable annuity contacts and
certificates and will be regulated by DFS through the newly created TIAA
Separate Account. Finally, section five provides the effective dates.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

TIAA was founded in 1918. In 1952, CREF was created as a companion
organization to TIAA through a special act of the Legislature to create
the world's first variable annuity. This legislation seeks to allow TIAA
to create a combined organization and continue its objective of modern-
izing the company for the benefit of its participants under the guidance
and oversight of DFS. This reorganization will have benefits for both
TIAA and CREF participants.

Currently, TIAA and CREF are governed under different statutory regimes
and we believe cannot be combined into one entity without an amendment
to CREF's enabling legislation. Our goal is to modernize and simplify
CREF's organizational structure. In the new structure, CREF will become
a separate account of TIAA regulated by DFS; this regulatory structure
is consistent with other insurance companies with separate accounts.

CREF's investments and operations will continue unchanged post the
proposed combination. In addition, CREF accounts will still be offered
"at-cost" without profit to TIAA. TIAA and CREF participants will also
benefit from operational efficiencies gained from streamlining the
organizational structure.

CREF participants will see a reduction in expenses when realized by TIAA
as a result of federal tax reduction attributes, deductions and foreign
tax credits which are only available to the combined entity.  Neither
TIAA nor CREF will be able to utilize this benefit without a combination
of the two entities. The conversion of CREF into a separate account of
TIAA will result in a simpler, more modern and more typical insurance
company and separate account structure and will eliminate the complex
regulatory anomaly of having TIM and CREF being legally independent but
closely aligned "companion" organizations. TIM, CREF and their partic-
ipants will benefit from this modernization effort as TIM emerges as a
more cost competitive entity which has a more transparent regulatory
framework.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S8126 - 2021/22

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

There are no fiscal impacts to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Effective immediately, except for section one which takes effect upon
filing DFS approval with the New York County Clerk.
